items.title: David Spinozza interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, NY, September 27, 2025
items.q: James Burton who played with Elvis Presley

ctx.x: Isn’t it interesting how, you know the music business has changed dramatically but the idea of, “Let’s start a band” is still there. Like what drives that? What drove you into this business?

Into the business of a band? Well when I was a kid I used to go to this place called the Canada Lounge which was in Mamaroneck, New York. And there was a band called The Orchids. And they were an R&B band. The guitar player was named Link Chamberlain. He was ahead of his time. He could bend the strings and do all this stuff that I’d never really heard. It was sort of almost like country – like country playing. And this was before light gauge strings, but Link had I guess became an expert at bending the string…

horns in that band. So they only had like two, so I said, “I’m going to have four.” So my band is going to have four horns. And that was the thing. And we also had choreography – we were like a show band. We did steps, we did all that kind of stuff. I was a showman, I used to front the band sometimes and dance. And sometimes I had a guitar player and I wouldn’t even play the guitar, I would just be the front man and I would sing and dance and I was all in to that whole thing in the beginning also.
